\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{வடிவமை} (vaṭivamai)}{வடிவமை (vaṭivamai)}]{\ta{வடிவமை} (vaṭivamai) — to design}

\label{lesson:TA-C551-vativamai}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for scaffolding, then the Tamil for a foreman.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{வடிவமை}}
\textbf{\ta{வடிவமை}} — \emph{vaṭivamai} — \textquotedblleft{}to design\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{என்} \ta{அக்கா} \ta{இந்த} \ta{வீட்டை} \ta{வடிவமைத்தாள்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{eṉ akkā inta vīṭṭai vaṭivamaittāḷ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My elder sister designed this house.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \ta{வடிவமைத்தேன்}, \emph{vaṭivamaittēṉ}.

The thing designed takes -\ta{ஐ}. A designer is a \ta{வடிவமைப்பாளர்}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{வடிவமை}} (\emph{vaṭivamai}) is a native compound: \ta{வடிவம்} (\emph{vaṭivam}), \textquotedblleft{}form, shape\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 5223), and \ta{அமை} (\emph{amai}), \textquotedblleft{}to arrange, to fit together\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 162).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vaṭivamai}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vaṭivamai}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{eṉ akkā inta vīṭṭai vaṭivamaittāḷ.} — My elder sister designed this house.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for scaffolding, then the Tamil for a foreman, then say \emph{vaṭivamai} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{வடிவமை} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To design\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{கான்கிரீட்} (kāṉkirīṭ)}{கான்கிரீட் (kāṉkirīṭ)}]{\ta{கான்கிரீட்} (kāṉkirīṭ) — concrete}

\label{lesson:TA-C551-kankirit}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a foreman, then the Tamil for to design.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{கான்கிரீட்}}
\textbf{\ta{கான்கிரீட்}} — \emph{kāṉkirīṭ} — \textquotedblleft{}concrete\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{பழைய} \ta{ஓட்டுக்} \ta{கூரைக்குப்} \ta{பதிலாகக்} \ta{கான்கிரீட்} \ta{கூரை} \ta{போட்டார்கள்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{paḻaiya ōṭṭuk kūraikkup patilākak kāṉkirīṭ kūrai pōṭṭārkaḷ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
They put a concrete roof in place of the old tiled roof.
\end{quote}

Written with the final \ta{ட்} of the English word.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{கான்கிரீட்}} (\emph{kāṉkirīṭ}) is a loan from English \emph{concrete}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāṉkirīṭ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāṉkirīṭ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paḻaiya ōṭṭuk kūraikkup patilākak kāṉkirīṭ kūrai pōṭṭārkaḷ.} — They put a concrete roof in place of the old tiled roof.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a foreman, then the Tamil for to design, then say \emph{kāṉkirīṭ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{கான்கிரீட்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Concrete\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{வேலி} (vēli)}{வேலி (vēli)}]{\ta{வேலி} (vēli) — a fence; a hedge}

\label{lesson:TA-C551-veli}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for to design, then the Tamil for concrete.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{வேலி}}
\textbf{\ta{வேலி}} — \emph{vēli} — \textquotedblleft{}a fence; a hedge\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{ஆடுகள்} \ta{உள்ளே} \ta{வராமல்} \ta{இருக்க} \ta{வேலி} \ta{போட்டோம்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āṭukaḷ uḷḷē varāmal irukka vēli pōṭṭōm.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We put up a fence to keep the goats from coming in.
\end{quote}

One puts up a fence with \ta{போடு} (\emph{pōṭu}): \ta{வேலி} \ta{போடு}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{வேலி}} (\emph{vēli}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 5538 gives \ta{வேலி} (\emph{vēli}), \textquotedblleft{}a fence, a hedge, a wall\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vēli}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vēli}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āṭukaḷ uḷḷē varāmal irukka vēli pōṭṭōm.} — We put up a fence to keep the goats from coming in.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for to design, then the Tamil for concrete, then say \emph{vēli} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{வேலி} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A fence; a hedge\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{சொத்து} (cottu)}{சொத்து (cottu)}]{\ta{சொத்து} (cottu) — property; assets}

\label{lesson:TA-C551-cottu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for concrete, then the Tamil for a fence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{சொத்து}}
\textbf{\ta{சொத்து}} — \emph{cottu} — \textquotedblleft{}property; assets\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{அவருடைய} \ta{சொத்து} \ta{முழுவதும்} \ta{பிள்ளைகளுக்குப்} \ta{போனது}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{avaruṭaiya cottu muḻuvatum piḷḷaikaḷukkup pōṉatu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
All his property went to his children.
\end{quote}

It covers land, houses and money. Inherited property is \ta{பரம்பரைச்} \ta{சொத்து}.

\begin{cousinweb}
The origin of \textbf{\ta{சொத்து}} (\emph{cottu}) is not settled: no dictionary we can check gives its source.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cottu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cottu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avaruṭaiya cottu muḻuvatum piḷḷaikaḷukkup pōṉatu.} — All his property went to his children.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for concrete, then the Tamil for a fence, then say \emph{cottu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{சொத்து} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Property; assets\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{யதார்த்தம்} (yatārttam)}{யதார்த்தம் (yatārttam)}]{\ta{யதார்த்தம்} (yatārttam) — reality}

\label{lesson:TA-C551-yatarttam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a fence, then the Tamil for property.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{யதார்த்தம்}}
\textbf{\ta{யதார்த்தம்}} — \emph{yatārttam} — \textquotedblleft{}reality\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{கனவு} \ta{வேறு}, \ta{யதார்த்தம்} \ta{வேறு}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kaṉavu vēṟu, yatārttam vēṟu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A dream is one thing, reality is another.
\end{quote}

With -\ta{ஆக}: \ta{யதார்த்தமாகப்} \ta{பேசு}, to speak realistically.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{யதார்த்தம்}} (\emph{yatārttam}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{yathārtha}, \textquotedblleft{}accordant with reality, true\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), with the Tamil ending -\ta{அம்}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yatārttam}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yatārttam}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaṉavu vēṟu, yatārttam vēṟu.} — A dream is one thing, reality is another.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a fence, then the Tamil for property, then say \emph{yatārttam} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{யதார்த்தம்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Reality\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from Stocks and Brokers to Designs and Property}

\label{lesson:TA-R551-review-545-551}



\begin{quote}
Say the Tamil for the stock market and a broker.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item the stock market, a broker, to lift up, considerably, a model
  \item a setback, a hindrance, an interruption, a stumbling block, to hold out
  \item to work out, to befall, to intend, to persist, to fix a date
  \item thrift, to go bankrupt, to swindle, a fraud, to break into
  \item a function hall, an agenda, a preview, readiness, to slip away
  \item a foundation, a brick, cement, scaffolding, a foreman
  \item to design, concrete, a fence, property, reality
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
The stock market? (\textbf{\ta{பங்குச்சந்தை}}, \emph{paṅkuccantai}.) A broker? (\textbf{\ta{தரகர்}}, \emph{tarakar}.) To lift up? (\textbf{\ta{உயர்த்து}}, \emph{uyarttu}.) Considerably? (\textbf{\ta{கணிசமாக}}, \emph{kaṇicamāka}.) A model? (\textbf{\ta{மாதிரி}}, \emph{mātiri}.) A setback? (\textbf{\ta{பின்னடைவு}}, \emph{piṉṉaṭaivu}.) A hindrance? (\textbf{\ta{இடையூறு}}, \emph{iṭaiyūṟu}.) An interruption? (\textbf{\ta{குறுக்கீடு}}, \emph{kuṟukkīṭu}.) A stumbling block? (\textbf{\ta{முட்டுக்கட்டை}}, \emph{muṭṭukkaṭṭai}.) To hold out? (\textbf{\ta{தாக்குப்பிடி}}, \emph{tākkuppiṭi}.) To work out? (\textbf{\ta{கைகூடு}}, \emph{kaikūṭu}.) To befall? (\textbf{\ta{நேரிடு}}, \emph{nēriṭu}.) To intend? (\textbf{\ta{உத்தேசி}}, \emph{uttēci}.) To persist? (\textbf{\ta{நீடி}}, \emph{nīṭi}.) To fix a date? (\textbf{\ta{நாள்} \ta{குறி}}, \emph{nāḷ kuṟi}.) Thrift? (\textbf{\ta{சிக்கனம்}}, \emph{cikkaṉam}.) To go bankrupt? (\textbf{\ta{திவாலாகு}}, \emph{tivālāku}.) To swindle? (\textbf{\ta{ஏய்}}, \emph{ēy}.) A fraud? (\textbf{\ta{மோசடி}}, \emph{mōcaṭi}.) To break into? (\textbf{\ta{ஊடுருவு}}, \emph{ūṭuruvu}.) A function hall? (\textbf{\ta{மண்டபம்}}, \emph{maṇṭapam}.) An agenda? (\textbf{\ta{நிகழ்ச்சிநிரல்}}, \emph{nikaḻcciniral}.) A preview? (\textbf{\ta{முன்னோட்டம்}}, \emph{muṉṉōṭṭam}.) Readiness? (\textbf{\ta{ஆயத்தம்}}, \emph{āyattam}.) To slip away? (\textbf{\ta{நழுவு}}, \emph{naḻuvu}.) A foundation? (\textbf{\ta{அஸ்திவாரம்}}, \emph{astivāram}.) A brick? (\textbf{\ta{செங்கல்}}, \emph{ceṅkal}.) Cement? (\textbf{\ta{சிமெண்ட்}}, \emph{cimeṇṭ}.) Scaffolding? (\textbf{\ta{சாரம்}}, \emph{cāram}.) A foreman? (\textbf{\ta{மேஸ்திரி}}, \emph{mēstiri}.) To design? (\textbf{\ta{வடிவமை}}, \emph{vaṭivamai}.) Concrete? (\textbf{\ta{கான்கிரீட்}}, \emph{kāṉkirīṭ}.) A fence? (\textbf{\ta{வேலி}}, \emph{vēli}.) Property? (\textbf{\ta{சொத்து}}, \emph{cottu}.) Reality? (\textbf{\ta{யதார்த்தம்}}, \emph{yatārttam}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
